Last week, Bloomberg said Apple is developing a screenless fitness tracker similar to the WHOOP or Fitbit Air. I have been using the WHOOP for the past six months and sincerely believe this is the right direction, but there are several aspects I hope Apple can do better.

Since the product is still in the early stages of development, we don't yet know the specific design of Apple's screenless fitness tracker, and it may not launch until as late as 2028. Bloomberg described it as "a slim fabric wristband with built-in sensors and computing modules."

Earlier this year, WHOOP partnered with Chase to offer discounts or free WHOOP devices to Sapphire credit card holders — I was one of the beneficiaries. I started using WHOOP around that time, but I haven't been able to fully commit to it.

The reason is simple: automatic workout detection is never perfect, and I find it quite cumbersome to specifically take out my phone to log a workout — whether before or after exercising. Apple Watch can start tracking directly from the watch face, while WHOOP can sync timing through Apple Health. This is also the main reason I continue to wear my Apple Watch.

If I'm going to the gym to work out, taking out my phone is acceptable, but if I'm just casually cycling or going for a walk, I don't want to have to take out my phone just to record it.

So for Apple's screenless fitness tracker, I sincerely hope they can add a combination of buttons and indicator lights to start and stop recording workouts. You'd still need to use your phone afterwards to categorize the activity type, but I'd rather do that after the workout than deal with it during. Apple could also develop categorization models based on various factors.

Summary

If Apple can successfully create a screenless fitness tracker that is easy to use and doesn't rely on a phone, I think it would be quite appealing. This design has several advantages, including more comfortable wear, longer battery life, and the ability to wear a traditional watch at the same time.

Personally, after evaluating the WHOOP, I actually lean more towards wearing a smartwatch, even if it means sacrificing battery life. I understand some people want a screenless design to avoid distractions, but for me, simply turning on the watch's "Do Not Disturb" mode solves that problem.

What do you think about Apple developing a screenless fitness tracker? How much would you be willing to pay for one? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
